title: Period functions for systems with homogeneous components
exact_target: Classify centers with unequal homogeneous component degrees and determine how often their periods can change monotonicity.
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
Fix nonnegative integers $k,\ell$ and nonzero real homogeneous polynomials
$P_{2k+1},Q_{2\ell+1}$ of the indicated degrees. Consider
\[
 \dot x=P_{2k+1}(x,y),\qquad
 \dot y=Q_{2\ell+1}(x,y).
\]
The origin is a center if it is an isolated equilibrium surrounded by a
punctured neighborhood foliated by periodic orbits. Its period annulus is
the maximal family of those surrounding closed orbits. Parameterize the
orbits by a smooth transversal, increasing away from the origin, and let
$T(s)$ be their least positive periods in the original time variable.

First, characterize the polynomial coefficient pairs for which the origin
is a center. Second, for each degree pair, determine the maximum number of
oscillations of $T$ on its full period annulus. In the critical-period
formulation this means bounding the isolated zeros of $T'(s)$; a change of
regular transverse coordinate does not change these zeros. A constant
period function is isochronous and is treated separately, not counted as
having infinitely many isolated critical periods.

The classification includes degenerate equilibria and is not restricted to
perturbations of a linear center. When $k=\ell$, homogeneity makes the
center condition and period scaling explicit; the genuinely different-degree
case is the main unresolved part. Statements about local extrema arbitrarily
close to the origin do not settle the requested global count, since further
stationary periods may occur near the outer boundary of the annulus.

\subsection{Short English statement}
Classify centers with unequal homogeneous component degrees and determine how often their periods can change monotonicity.
